title: HyperLogLogLog: Cardinality Estimation With One Log More

problem.claim: Estimate the number of distinct elements n using an m-register HyperLogLog sketch while reducing its space usage.

contributions.claim: HyperLogLogLog compresses the HyperLogLog sketch from O(m log log n) bits to m log_2 log_2 log_2 m + O(m + log log n) bits.
The compressed sketch supports conversion to and from the uncompressed representation, compressed-domain merging, and amortized constant-time updates when n is sufficiently larger than m.
A corollary gives a theoretical compression algorithm using m log_2 log_2 log_2 log_2 m + O(m log log log m / log log m + log log n) bits.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the compressed sketch preserves all estimation properties of HyperLogLog and maintains mergeability in the compressed domain.
In experimental comparisons with well-known Google and Apache implementations, the authors report small sketches with competitive update and merge times.
The authors observed an approximately 40% reduction in sketch size.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces HyperLogLogLog as a compressed HyperLogLog sketch with substantially lower stated space complexity.
Describes representation conversion, preserved estimation properties, compressed-domain mergeability, and the update-time condition.
Provides a C++ implementation and reports comparisons showing small sketches and competitive update and merge times.
Reports an approximately 40% reduction in sketch size.
States a further theoretical compression bound as a corollary.

source_observation.claim: A compressed sketch can retain estimation properties, conversion, and mergeability while reducing its representation size.

interpretation.claim: Compression is more useful when it preserves the operational interface and distributed-computation behavior of the original sketch.

application.claim: When compressing a mergeable data structure, preserve conversions and native merge operations so adoption can remain compatible with existing workflows.

exception.claim: The reported amortized constant-time update guarantee assumes n is sufficiently larger than m.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the estimation error metrics or experimental datasets.
The abstract does not define how large n must be relative to m for the update-time guarantee.
The abstract does not provide proof details for the stated bounds.
